title: Primary science: Earth and space
description: Four lessons on day-night, seasons, moon phases and the water cycle: order cycles, explain causes, and transfer to new observations.
assumptions: Qualitative cycles and causes; no numeric astronomy required.
stage2goal: Explain causes and transfer to observations.
day-night.title: Day and night: Earth spins
day-night.goal: Order the day-night cycle and attribute it to Earth’s spin.
day-night.reading: Earth spins once a day; the side facing the Sun has day, the other night. The Sun does not move around Earth.
day-night.worked.prompt: Why does your town have day then night?
day-night.worked.fb: Earth spins, turning your town toward then away from the Sun.
day-night.worked.content: Earth’s spin carries your town into light then shadow.
day-night.order.n1.label: night
day-night.order.d.label: day
day-night.order.n2.label: night again
day-night.independent.a.label: Earth spinning
day-night.independent.b.label: Sun orbiting Earth
day-night.c1.a.label: one Earth orbit of Sun
day-night.c1.b.label: one Earth spin
seasons.title: Seasons: tilt, not distance
seasons.goal: Attribute seasons to Earth’s tilt, not distance to Sun.
seasons.reading: Earth’s axis is tilted; the hemisphere tilted toward the Sun gets summer. Distance is not the cause.
seasons.struggle: Without numbers, explain why it is summer in the north when the north tilts toward the Sun.
seasons.worked.prompt: Why does tilt toward the Sun mean summer?
seasons.worked.fb: More direct light and longer days.
seasons.worked.content: Tilt toward Sun → direct light, long days → summer.
seasons.order.sp.label: spring
seasons.order.su.label: summer
seasons.order.au.label: autumn
seasons.order.wi.label: winter
seasons.transfer-hemisphere.prompt: When north has summer, south has…
seasons.transfer-hemisphere.a.label: summer too
seasons.transfer-hemisphere.b.label: winter
seasons.c1.a.label: axis tilt
seasons.c1.b.label: distance to Sun
moon-phases.title: Moon phases: lit half we see
moon-phases.goal: Order moon phases and explain we see varying lit portions.
moon-phases.reading: The Sun always lights half the Moon; as the Moon orbits Earth we see different portions of that lit half.
moon-phases.worked.prompt: Why does the Moon look different each week?
moon-phases.worked.fb: We see different portions of the lit half.
moon-phases.worked.content: Moon orbits Earth; our view of the lit half changes.
moon-phases.order.prompt: Order: new moon / full moon / new moon again.
moon-phases.order.n1.label: new moon
moon-phases.order.f.label: full moon
moon-phases.order.n2.label: new moon again
moon-phases.transfer-phase.fb: Earth between Sun and Moon (lit side faces us).
moon-phases.transfer-phase.a.label: lit side fully faces us
moon-phases.transfer-phase.b.label: Moon stops orbiting
moon-phases.c1.a.label: only the full moon
moon-phases.c1.b.label: half the Moon always
water-cycle.title: The water cycle
water-cycle.reading: Sun heats water → evaporation; vapor cools → condensation (clouds); drops fall → precipitation; water returns to start.
water-cycle.worked.prompt: Why does a puddle disappear on a sunny day?
water-cycle.worked.fb: Sun heat evaporates it into vapor.
water-cycle.worked.content: Sunny heat turns puddle water to vapor.
water-cycle.order.p.label: precipitation
water-cycle.order.e.label: evaporation
water-cycle.order.c.label: condensation
water-cycle.transfer-cloud.a.label: evaporation
water-cycle.transfer-cloud.b.label: condensation
water-cycle.c1.a.label: precipitation
water-cycle.c1.b.label: condensation
water-cycle.c2.prompt: The water cycle is driven by…
water-cycle.c2.a.label: wind only
water-cycle.c2.b.label: Sun heat
